html:
SMTO-GML-0028 — SMTO can't handle Gmail attachments outside a conversation

GUID: 8e6a0b67-4a28-47f2-9864-e608ea2a4654
Slug: gmail-task-artifact-context-required
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO tried to save an email attachment or attach a file to an email, but this request isn't connected to a conversation where SMTO can keep or find files. Nothing was saved or sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open a conversation in SMTO and ask there to save the attachment or attach a file to the email. SMTO keeps files with the conversation that asked for them, so the request needs a conversation.
  2. To send a file, first add it to that same conversation, or use a file SMTO made earlier in it. SMTO only attaches files that belong to the conversation, to keep other people's files private.
  3. If this happens again inside a normal conversation, select Copy error details. Inside a conversation SMTO should always have a place for files, so this points to a problem the person who manages SMTO needs to see.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the saved attachment as a file in the conversation, or reports the email with its attachment as created or sent.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to attach a file from a different conversation as a workaround.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gmail attachment operation lacked file context: saving or exporting attachments/messages had no artifact store or run_id, or resolving outgoing attachments had no artifact store or conversation_id.

What this means

  • Attachment publication lacks an artifact store/run scope, or outgoing attachment resolution lacks a store/conversation grant scope. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Attachment publication lacks an artifact store/run scope, or outgoing attachment resolution lacks a store/conversation grant scope.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the owning run/conversation and existing artifact grants rather than supplying an arbitrary filesystem path.

How to fix it

  • files.save_attachment and client_actions.files (download_attachments, export_messages) require context['_artifact_store'] and _artifact_scope.run_id; _outgoing_attachments requires _artifact_store and _artifact_scope.conversation_id. These are bound by artifacts.runtime.bind for agent Runs, so invoke the Gmail tools from a conversation Run and reference files granted to that conversation rather than another conversation's files; if this occurs inside a normal Run, inspect why the artifact scope was not bound.
  • Use the owning task and its authorized artifact context for the attachment.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended attachment operation runs inside its supported authorized artifact context.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
